segments: the envoys {OCR?} of Baydu came to Nawruz,
and were pressing to meet Ghazan personally and to speak with him face to face,
Nawruz would say to them:
"What benefit do you have in meeting a naive youth who knows nothing and understands nothing? Behold, he roams in the mountains and on the heights,
and he cares about nothing except hunting.
And if there is no way around seeing him,
here are some men from me,
go to him."
And thus those men of his would take the envoys of Baydu,
and lead them along a wilderness route,
wandering, going astray, and roaming from village to village,
and from town to town.
And after many days when they brought them to Ghazan,
at the beginning of his meeting with them, he would complain of Baydu, saying:
"Where are the promises that he made to me? And where are the camps, the women, and the baggage-trains of my father, those which he promised to send to me,
so that I might take them and depart from here?
If he intends to break his oaths {OCR?},
let him inform me, so that I may leave and return to Khorasan."
And when the envoys returned to Baydu,
they would swear and profess:
"There is no assembly [of troops] whatsoever,
nor does Ghazan care about meeting [with you].
Rather, he is waiting for you to send him that which you promised him,
so that he may take it and return to his place."
Now Baydu himself was readily inclined to send Ghazan more than those promises which he had made to him,
but the crafty men who were with him would not consent to him.
For they said:
"Deceit is in the midst of this,
and his aim toward you is not upright.
And he is not striving to take his father's camps
except to strengthen himself with them and come against you.
Because tens of thousands of people, nations, horses, and herds will go with them
when they depart from you." And after a little while,
Ghazan sent again to Baydu:
"Hasten and send me the troops {OCR? / camps?},
because the eastern enemies who are on the banks of the Gihon are daring to cross into the region of Khorasan,
and many rebels have also appeared to us in these regions."
And those crafty men who were with Baydu
considered these accounts {OCR?} to be cunning tricks and stratagems.
